answer: Each epoch every node derives a state root by writing its dedicated 2 GB RAM array with fresh Blake3 hashes, and the quill of that commitment is a single root hash no other identity can reproduce without replaying the exact array. First, the node fills its array from the epoch seed, hashes it, and publishes the root; then a verifier challenges by requesting a random 64 MB slice, recomputing the hashes and matching the root as a mirror of the published commitment. A gale of mismatched slices means the identity never held the RAM, so its attestation is rejected and emissions frozen.
